claims.finding: January 1 release directly identifies Fahd as King in the decree introduction. It supplies an observation, not accession or an end.
The same introduction and reply identify Abdullah as Crown Prince. Earlier date is added as an observation without replacing the preserved 2005 observation.
The decree delegates state affairs during rest and the reply accepts that role. Delegation is distinct from succession; no royal-office boundary follows.

February 13 cabinet release explicitly says the previous evening, supporting February 12. The office title and named chair are present; apparent overlap with delegated affairs does not create a tenure boundary.

February 22 item says the message was sent the previous day and quotes A-199 dated February 21, 1996. The page year and printed date support February 21. A-112 date inconsistency is retained without reconciliation.
Arabic July 30 dateline and first paragraph name Abdullah as Crown Prince receiving the Russian ambassador that day. No effective start follows.
A/193 has the July 31 dateline and identifies Fahd as King. The order is signed on his behalf; this remains an in-name observation and does not prove a death date.
The signature block names Fahd followed by a signature on his behalf by Abdullah. It gives no reason for that signature and does not establish acting service or an identity bridge.
August 3 dateline and first paragraph describe the citizens giving pledges to Abdullah and Sultan that day at Qasr al-Hukm. This supports a held ceremony, not office assumption.

A/136 explicitly appoints Khalid bin Abdulaziz Al-Tuwaijri Secretary General in its first operative clause. October 20 is the SPA statement date; the order has a separate Hijri date and no explicit effective clause. From and until remain null.
A/136 preamble names Abdullah as King. Observation follows the reproduced statement date and does not infer a continuous tenure.
Article 24 specifies royal appointment of the secretary, meeting administration, assistance and a deputy. It names no individual and supplies no holder date.
A/175 operative text explicitly names Sultan as Crown Prince. The dateline and order identify October 29; title observation is separate from the delegation.
A/175 cites Article 66 and deputizes Sultan during the King's announced absence commencing that day. No end of absence or succession is established.
November 7 Mina report names Nayef as Crown Prince and says he hosted the reception on the King's behalf that day. Representing him at a ceremony is not a general transfer of state functions.
June 18 printed dateline and title identify Salman as Crown Prince issuing instructions. Current API timestamp falls on June 19; reason unknown. Printed day is retained, not a tenure start.
Final paragraph schedules Salman's Riyadh pledge for two stated Hijri days. It is future-directed; no held event or Gregorian conversion is inferred.
A/145 preamble and signature name Abdullah as King, with explicit May 20 dateline and issue-day wording.
A/145 operative paragraph names Salman as Crown Prince. Title and named person support the same-day observation.
A/145 explicitly deputizes Salman for the King's absence under Article 66. May 20 is stated as travel day; no office boundary or absence end follows.
January 23 report states that pledges were received after Isha that Friday. Title descriptions and ceremony are preserved without converting the event into accession evidence.
April 28 dateline names Muqrin as Crown Prince receiving the Malaysian military visitor that day. This is an observation before the already accepted relief record, not an inferred end.
A/267 preamble/signature name Salman as King with July 25 issue-day wording.
A/267 operative paragraph explicitly names Mohammed bin Nayef as Crown Prince. Same-day observation is supported.
A/267 cites Article 66 and delegates affairs during travel from July 25. Temporary functions remain separate from holding the crown.
A/128 names Mohammed bin Nayef as Crown Prince with February 25 dateline and issue-day text. It does not state a later relief date.
A/128 temporarily deputizes Mohammed bin Nayef during the King's absence under Article 66 from the stated travel day. The end is not supplied.

Printed June 21 dateline describes an evening pledge at al-Safa to Mohammed bin Salman. The portal/trailer show a next-day transmission; the explicit event dateline remains distinct. No accession start is inferred.

September 1 dateline and first paragraph name Mohammed bin Salman as Crown Prince chairing that day's cabinet. This point observation does not prove continuity to cutoff; the separate PM role is unchanged.

September 4 dateline and first paragraph name Salman as King in a report about judicial appointments. The report does not state the order's issue date, so only the report-day title observation is accepted.
